explainBack.question: Why could a note another agent posted on the wiki change a later agent's answer, even if the model was never retrained?
explainBack.answer: Because whatever a web tool fetches while the agent works is added to the model's context — the information supplied during the task. The model uses that context together with its already-learned patterns to produce its response. So a shared note about Nevada can steer the next answer immediately, while the model's learned patterns (built during training) remain untouched. Better answers via shared notes are a change in inputs, not proof of a changed model.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: P008 supplies the fetch-note-enters-context-influences-answer chain and defines model and training; P009 draws the explicit consequence for 'AI improving itself' claims.
explainBack.assessment: The article's mechanism fully supports this answer in ordinary language; the explain-back succeeds without importing outside knowledge.

unseenTransfer.scenario: An insurance firm gives its customer-service AI assistants read access to a shared internal FAQ page that staff and other assistants keep updated. Someone posts an outdated premium figure there. Over the next week, three different assistants quote the same wrong premium to customers, and a manager takes the agreement of three systems as confirmation the figure is right.
unseenTransfer.question: Using the article's mechanism, why do the three matching answers not confirm the premium, and what should the manager check?
unseenTransfer.answer: Each assistant's tool fetched the same FAQ note, so the wrong figure entered each one's context and shaped each answer — three outputs, one source, exactly the single-source-agreement trap in P012. Nothing about the assistants' models changed; their inputs converged. The manager should ask what each assistant could read (P011) and trace the premium back to the original rate document rather than the shared page.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: P008 (fetched contents enter context and influence answers), P011 (ask what information was available), P012 (matching answers resting on one source; trace to original evidence).
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's mechanism transfers cleanly to this new situation with no gaps; the reader is equipped to reason it through.
